prompt.context: Our client, GGC Health, operates eight Ambulatory Surgical Centers (ASC) on the east coast. GGC Health has consistently been a profitable organization, but over the past two years, their ASCs' cumulative revenues have been flat at $400 million/year. The CEO of GGC Health is concerned about this and has hired your firm to increase revenues by 15%.
prompt.question: How would you help GGC Health increase revenues by 15%?

clarifying_info.a: ASCs are modern health care facilities focused on providing same-day surgical care, including diagnostic and preventive procedures. They are seen as a more convenient alternative to hospital-based outpatient procedures.

clarifying_info.q: Who decides where surgeries are performed?
clarifying_info.a: Physicians generally dictate where the surgery is performed. They can perform surgeries at hospitals or ASCs.

clarifying_info.q: How does GGC Health generate revenue?
clarifying_info.a: ASC revenue is equal to the number of procedures performed in the facility multiplied by the expected reimbursement per procedure.

exhibits.title: Physician Group Membership by City
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing the percentage breakdown of physician specialties (Orthopedic, Neurology, Gastroenterology) for three cities: Charlotte, Indianapolis, and Nashville.

exhibits.title: Average Reimbursement Rates Per Patient by Specialty
exhibits.shows: A table listing physician specialties and their corresponding reimbursement rate per patient.

framework: Increase revenue at existing 8 ASCs: grow number of patients per doctor, grow number of doctors per facility, optimize procedure/product mix toward higher-reimbursement specialties, expand types of patients (payer mix)

Increase revenue by opening new ASCs: analyze market opportunity in target cities, evaluate physician group partnerships, assess patient demographics for common ASC surgeries, analyze competitors and regulatory/reimbursement environment

questions.prompt: GGC Health has researched three expansion cities: Charlotte (30 doctors), Indianapolis (25 doctors), and Nashville (16 doctors). Given management can only open one ASC immediately, which city should they enter? Use Exhibit 1.
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply total doctors in each city by the specialty breakdown from Exhibit 1 to get doctors per specialty per city. An excellent candidate will quickly eliminate Nashville because Indianapolis has more doctors in every specialty than Nashville. Charlotte vs. Indianapolis comparison sets up the revenue calculation in Q2.

math.setup: Doctors per specialty = total doctors in city * specialty percentage from Exhibit 1
steps: Nashville eliminated: Indianapolis has more doctors in every specialty (Ortho 10 vs 8, Neuro 10 vs 4, Gastro 5 vs 4)
math.answer: Charlotte and Indianapolis remain; Nashville is eliminated.

questions.prompt: Orthopedic brings in 15 patients per doctor per month, neurology is 10, and gastroenterology is 12. Ask for reimbursement rates (Exhibit 2). Calculate total annual revenue for Charlotte and Indianapolis to determine the most attractive city, and check whether it meets the $60M target.
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate patients per year per specialty, multiply by reimbursement rate to get revenue per doctor per year, then multiply by number of doctors per specialty per city and sum. Should identify Indianapolis as most attractive but note it falls short of the $60M target alone (~$49.8M vs $60M needed).

math.setup: Revenue per doctor per year = (patients/doctor/month * 12) * reimbursement rate/patient; City revenue = sum over specialties of (doctors in specialty * revenue per doctor per year)
steps: Revenue per doctor per year: Ortho = 15*12*$5,000 = $900K | Neuro = 10*12*$25,000 = $3M | Gastro = 12*12*$15,000 = $2.16M
math.answer: Indianapolis is the most attractive city at $49.8M annual revenue, but it alone does not meet the $60M revenue target.

questions.prompt: Indianapolis alone does not achieve the desired revenue growth. Brainstorm how GGC Health could increase revenues at their current 8 ASC locations to close the gap.
questions.guidance: Candidate should be structured and organized. Strong answers cover: (1) increasing patients per doctor — make ASC the preferred venue by offering more control, better scheduling, enhanced efficiency, better outcomes; prioritize high-volume doctors; profit-sharing incentives for hitting targets. (2) Increasing doctors per ASC — recruit new physicians, add new procedure types with new physician groups, improve physician outreach/marketing. (3) Optimizing product/payer mix — prioritize high-reimbursement surgeries, add new high-reimbursement procedure types, review Medicaid/Medicare acceptance, target patients with higher reimbursements.

questions.prompt: GGC Health's current 8 ASC sites do not offer urology. They can add 2 urology doctors to all current ASC sites. Each doctor brings in 8 patients per doctor per month. Calculate the additional revenue from this initiative.
questions.guidance: Candidate should use Exhibit 2 for the urology reimbursement rate ($8,000). Should recognize additional revenue applies only to the current 8 sites. Incremental same-site revenue from urology plus new Indianapolis ASC together meet the $60M target ($12M + $49.8M = $61.8M).

math.setup: Total urologists = 8 sites * 2 urologists/site; patients/year = total urologists * (patients/doctor/month * 12); revenue = patients/year * reimbursement rate
steps: Combined with Indianapolis: $49.8M + $12M = $61.8M, which exceeds the $60M target
math.answer: $12M additional revenue from urology; combined with Indianapolis ASC ($49.8M), total new revenue is ~$61.8M, meeting the $60M target.

brainstorming.prompt: How can GGC Health increase revenues at their current 8 ASC locations?

categories.name: Increase patients per doctor
ideas: Make ASC the preferred surgical venue by offering physicians more control over the environment
Improve scheduling flexibility and operational efficiency
Demonstrate better patient outcomes vs. hospital-based outpatient settings
Provide doctors with a higher profit share for hitting volume targets
Prioritize onboarding and retaining high-volume doctors

categories.name: Increase doctors per ASC
ideas: Recruit physicians in new specialties (e.g., urology, dermatology, pain management)
Add new procedure types and bring in physician groups that perform them
Launch improved physician outreach and sales/marketing efforts

categories.name: Optimize product and payer mix
ideas: Prioritize scheduling for high-reimbursement surgeries (neurology, gastroenterology)
Add new high-reimbursement procedure types not currently offered
Review and expand Medicaid/Medicare acceptance where reimbursement is favorable
Target patients whose payers offer higher reimbursement rates

recommendation: Open a new ASC in Indianapolis, generating approximately $49.8M in incremental annual revenue
Add 2 urology doctors to each of the 8 existing ASC sites, generating approximately $12M in incremental annual revenue — together these initiatives deliver ~$61.8M, exceeding the $60M (15%) target
risks: No cost analysis was conducted for the new Indianapolis facility or for adding urology — profitability is unconfirmed
Indianapolis is not on the east coast; management is unfamiliar with the Midwest market
Existing ASCs may lack capacity to accommodate new urology surgeries immediately
Actual physician volume and market share may fall short of projections
Physicians may not bring in the expected number of patients per month
next_steps: Conduct a full cost/benefit analysis for the Indianapolis location before committing
If Indianapolis proves lucrative, begin site selection and construction planning
Add urology surgeries to current ASCs as soon as possible
Evaluate other high-reimbursement specialties to add across existing sites
Assess feasibility of opening more than one new location in the future
